description: One hour of raw location samples and activity changes recorded by one device.

main.description:
One hour of raw location samples and activity changes recorded by one device. The record key is the UTC hour and the device's identifier joined by a colon, such as 2026-10-19T14:6f1c2b0e-8a4d-4f3e-9b21-5c7d8e9f0a1b, so a new sample only rewrites the current hour. When an hour holds more than one record's limits allow, the device starts another part keyed with :2, :3 and so on after that (see part). Visits and journeys aren't stored: every device works them out from these samples.

New samples come only from the recording device, but another device can rewrite the record to delete samples. The first write of a record (a new hour, or a new part) is create-only (createOnly), and every later write is conditional on the version the device last read (swapCid). A device whose write is refused reads the record again, merges and retries. Merging two versions of a record gives: samples = every sample in either version, minus every id in either version's deletedSampleIds; transitions likewise with deletedTransitionIds; and both deletion lists = everything in either version. Deletion lists only grow.

Deleting a sample removes it from the samples of the part that holds it and lists its id in that same part's deletedSampleIds, never in another part, so the deleted location is gone from the stored record. Deleting an activity change works the same way with transitions and deletedTransitionIds.

device.description: Identifier of the device that recorded the samples.

startsAt.description: The start of the UTC hour the samples fall in, such as 2026-10-19T14:00:00.000Z.

part.description: Which part of the hour this record is, when the hour needed more than one. Absent for the first part, whose key has no part number. Parts after the first have keys ending in :2, :3 and so on. A device adds new samples and activity changes to the last part. It starts the next part as soon as the last part's samples plus deletedSampleIds reach 5,000, or its transitions plus deletedTransitionIds reach 500. A sample in a part can only move to that part's deletion list, so a part's deletion lists never outgrow their limits.

samples.description: The location samples, in time order. The limits on this record's lists are set so that, with every field at its longest, the record still fits in one sealed record (about 3.99 MB).

transitions.description: Changes in what the person was doing that the device detected, such as starting to walk, in time order.

deletedSampleIds.description: Ids of samples from this hour that the person deleted. A device must not add a sample back once its id is listed here.

deletedTransitionIds.description: Ids of activity changes from this hour that were deleted. A device must not add one back once its id is listed here.

id.description: Identifier of the sample, unique for the account. Corrections and deletions refer to the sample by this value.

altitudeMeters.description: Decimal meters above the WGS84 ellipsoid.

accuracyCentimeters.description: Horizontal accuracy, in centimeters: the device's value in meters times 100, rounded to the nearest whole number with halves away from zero, and 0 if it was negative. Left out when the value is NaN or infinite.

speedCentimetersPerSecond.description: Speed, in centimeters per second: the device's value in meters per second times 100, rounded to the nearest whole number with halves away from zero, and 0 if it was negative. Left out when the value is NaN or infinite.

bearingCentidegrees.description: Direction of travel in hundredths of a degree, clockwise from true north: the device's value in degrees times 100, rounded to the nearest whole number with halves away from zero, then reduced with a true modulo into 0 to 35999 whatever its sign or size (359.996 degrees becomes 0, -0.01 becomes 35999, -360.5 becomes 35950). Left out when the value is NaN or infinite. The conversion rules are in docs/reference/lexicon-style.md.

activity.description: How the person was moving when the sample was taken. vehicle means some vehicle whose kind isn't known; driving, bus and train are specific kinds. Defaults to unknown.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone the device was in when it took the sample.

source.description: What made the device take the sample, such as a periodic background check or writing an entry. Defaults to unknown.

mock.description: True when the device reported a simulated location.

transition.description: The moment the device detected that the person started or stopped an activity, such as walking or riding in a vehicle. LogDate uses these to find where visits begin and end.

id.description: Identifier of the activity change, unique for the account.

activity.description: The activity, as the device's activity recognition reported it. onFoot means walking or running without knowing which.

transition.description: Whether the person started (enter) or stopped (exit) the activity.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone the device was in at the time.
